title: Flock municipal cancellations & non-renewals catalog

scope_note: Index of catalogued municipal/agency actions for the on-site lookup table. Full writeups live on national.html. Not a complete national census. Older aggregator tallies (for example a May 2026 82-contract count) can be smaller than this list.

records.Primary_Reasons: Public backlash / privacy; Commission 18-0 non-renewal; Prior sheriff suspend
records.Summary: Sheriff Jeffrey Cassidy suspended the Sullivan County Sheriff’s Office’s 10 Flock cameras on August 17, 2026. On August 20 the County Commission voted 18–0 not to renew the Flock contract. WJHL (via Yahoo) reported the resolution was amended to say Flock cameras would not be used within the county, excluding Kingsport and Bristol police cameras. The contract ends in January 2027. Elections administrator Jason Booher said the commission cannot place Cassidy’s requested referendum on the ballot.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Sheriff use already suspended. County non-renewal takes effect when the contract ends in January 2027. Does not apply to Kingsport or Bristol PD cameras. Nearby and private Flock can continue.

records.Primary_Reasons: Public backlash / privacy; Data-access concerns; Council vote to shut cameras immediately and cancel the contract
records.Summary: Gardner City Council on August 17, 2026 agreed to turn off the city’s Flock cameras immediately and not renew the contract. KMBC reported August 18 that some cameras were covered by Tuesday, and that Gardner Police confirmed it discontinued all city Flock cameras and notified the vendor the contract was canceled. Council member Kelly Johnson said the vote covers only city-controlled cameras, not Johnson County or state units nearby. Resident Bradley Steinmetz of No Flock in Gardner said more than 1,200 vendors had access through the Flock system.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Camera count not published. County and state ALPRs in and around Gardner remain. Physical pickup timetable not published.

records.Primary_Reasons: Public backlash; Mass-surveillance / Fourth Amendment / data-security concerns; Packed council meeting; Mayor terminate decision
records.Summary: After residents packed the August 17, 2026 council meeting, Fort Mitchell Mayor Greg Pohlgeers said the city would shut off and dismantle its five Flock readers immediately and would not renew. LINK nky reported the 2024 contract was 24 months for about $34,000. City Administrator Edwin King said staff would coordinate with Flock to end operations. FOX19 reported the mayor’s overnight announcement on August 19.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Immediate shutdown announced; vendor pickup timetable not published.

records.Primary_Reasons: Budget cuts; Public trust / privacy concerns; Police announcement to council; Related ODOT ALPR agreement killed
records.Summary: Winston Police Chief Brandon Sarti told City Council on August 17, 2026 that the department had canceled its Flock contract that day. NR Today reported eight cameras in Douglas County at about $24,000 a year, amid $215,000 in department budget cuts. Sarti said the lieutenant’s retirement plus the cancel should save about $217,000, and that if residents paying the bill do not want the cameras, the city is turning them off. Council also killed proposed Resolution 26-1237, an ODOT intergovernmental agreement that would have allowed ALPRs on Oregon Route 42. Mayor Christie Knutson said community outcry was part of the removal.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Physical removal timetable not published in the NR Today report.

records.Primary_Reasons: Officer alleged personal Flock / CJIS lookups; Police chief ended the Flock relationship as a direct result; Last camera removed
records.Summary: Stow Police Chief Michael Sallese announced August 18, 2026 that the department ended its Flock relationship as a direct result of alleged personal Flock and CJIS lookups by a Stow officer. The Boston Globe and boston.com reported the last remaining Flock camera was removed in early August; two other ALPRs came down earlier in 2026 after an effectiveness review. See FLK-2026-048. The department said it will evaluate safeguards before any future ALPR use and will bring a tighter request/approval policy to the Select Board.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Last camera removed early August 2026; two others removed earlier in 2026. Department may request ALPR data from outside agencies under a forthcoming policy.

records.Primary_Reasons: Privacy / constitutional concerns; National misuse reports; Sheriff suspend and dismantle while contract runs through 2028
records.Summary: Henry County Sheriff Wayne Davis suspended sheriff’s-office access to 14 Flock cameras (10 fixed, 4 mobile) on August 14, 2026 and said the office would explore early termination of a contract that runs through August 2028. WSLS reported August 17 that the office would begin dismantling the cameras in the coming days. Davis had said in July he would not renew in 2028; the August suspend moved that timeline up. This is a suspend / hardware pull, not a reported contract termination.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Contract still runs through August 2028. WSLS quoted Davis saying cameras may still record while sheriff’s-office access is off. Physical removal was announced as beginning in the days after August 17.

records.Primary_Reasons: Privacy / data-retention concerns; National ALPR backlash; Chief non-renewal pending 2027 legislative standards
records.Summary: Waukee Police Chief Chad McCluskey announced August 14, 2026 that the department will not renew its Flock Safety ALPR contract and will stop using the cameras pending the 2027 Iowa legislative session. The Des Moines Register reported 11 cameras and that none had been vandalized locally. Waukee was the first Des Moines metro city reported to drop Flock; Coralville canceled earlier in 2026.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Non-renewal / stop-use pending state legislation. Hardware removal timetable not published. Neighboring metro cities still contract with Flock per Register reporting.

records.Primary_Reasons: Privacy / data-sharing concerns; Public trust review; Chief deactivate pending legislative standards
records.Summary: Indianola Police Chief Rob Hawkins announced that beginning August 17, 2026 the department deactivated its eight Flock cameras and disabled outside-agency access to the data. KCRG and the Des Moines Register reported the program costs about $24,000 a year. Cameras remain installed pending coordination with Flock. Untied data will purge in 30 days. The department said it is listening to privacy concerns and watching the 2027 legislative session.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Suspend / deactivate, not a reported contract termination. Hardware remains up pending vendor coordination. May resume after review or 2027 legislation.

records.Primary_Reasons: Constitutional / privacy / public-trust concerns; Sheriff non-renewal after grant pilot; Fiscal responsibility
records.Summary: Henry County, Missouri, Sheriff Aaron N. Brown announced August 10, 2026 that the sheriff’s office will not renew its Flock Safety LPR agreement when the current term expires March 11, 2027. The program began earlier in 2026 through a State of Missouri grant. Brown said the system assisted investigations in its first five months but that public trust and constitutional principles weighed against continuing past the grant term.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Operational through March 11, 2027. Camera count not published in the Aug. 10 statement. Distinct from Henry County, Virginia (CAN-2026-105).

records.Primary_Reasons: Massachusetts procurement-law deficiencies; Town legal review; Privacy / ALPR concerns at Select Board
records.Summary: The Town of Hopkinton announced August 20, 2026 that it terminated its Flock Safety contract immediately after a legal review found statutory deficiencies that make the agreement unlawful under Massachusetts law. Town Manager Elaine Lazarus said municipal contracts must comply with procurement law. The town asked Flock to turn the cameras off as soon as possible and remove them by September 30. Two cameras had been up about five months; two more had been planned.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Town asked for cameras off ASAP and physical removal by Sept. 30, 2026. Town plans a broader review of Hopkinton PD technology, including ALPRs.

records.Primary_Reasons: Public backlash / privacy; Outside-agency data sharing; Council 6-1 terminate vote
records.Summary: Oxford City Council voted 6–1 on August 18, 2026 to terminate the police department’s Flock contract. Councilmember Bill Snavely, who offered the legislation, cited how other departments would use shared data. WVXU reported August 19 that the council considered a Police Community Relations Review Commission recommendation to keep the contract with tighter sharing, then followed resident opposition. Police Chief John Jones was to notify Flock. Nearby Hamilton residents protested the same day; Hamilton has not canceled.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Camera count not published. Physical removal timetable not published; Snavely said Flock could turn cameras off and remove them or the city could bag them. Hamilton, Ohio, has not canceled.

records.Primary_Reasons: Public trust / data-privacy concerns; Sheriff end partnership; Citizen concern
records.Summary: Henry County, Illinois, Sheriff Josh Verscheure announced August 19, 2026 that the sheriff’s office will end its Flock partnership on August 31. KWQC reported the cameras arrived in 2024, funded with drug-seizure proceeds rather than county tax dollars. Verscheure said the office saw no local misuse in two years and that Flock had helped investigations, but that public-trust and data-privacy concerns outweighed continuing. Distinct from Henry County, Virginia, and Henry County, Missouri.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Partnership ends August 31, 2026. Camera count not published. Distinct from Henry County, Virginia (CAN-2026-105) and Henry County, Missouri (CAN-2026-108).

records.Primary_Reasons: Data-security / search-log leaks; Privacy; Non-renewal while shopping a replacement vendor
records.Summary: The Abington Township Police Department is ending its Flock contracts over data-security concerns after thousands of the department’s searches appeared in public dumps, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported August 19, 2026. One contract expired in August 2026; the department will let the second expire in February 2028. Officials said they are negotiating with other vendors to replace Flock. This is an expire / vendor-swap path, not a clear exit from ALPR.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: One contract expired August 2026; second runs to February 2028. Department is seeking a replacement ALPR vendor. One permanent camera plus portable units kept at the station. Not a clear exit from plate readers.

records.Primary_Reasons: Public backlash / privacy; Commission rescind of April 2025 authorization; Prior budget defund
records.Summary: The White County Commission voted July 20, 2026 to rescind the April 2025 resolution that authorized Flock license-plate cameras. UCNOW reported Chair Derrick Hutchings cited resident privacy pushback. In June the commission had already stripped about $48,000 in Flock funding while leaving the dollars in the sheriff’s budget. Hutchings said the sheriff’s office initiated the contract, cameras went up around September or October 2025, and they likely still collect data while standing. Sparta cameras are a separate city program.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Hardware may still be standing and recording. After the June funding strip, Sheriff Steve Page told Flock the county cameras were unfunded and could come down (Sparta Live, July 17, 2026). On August 7, 2026, the Upper Cumberland News Leader quoted Page saying he ordered Flock removal after community feedback; pickup/removal confirmation still waits on reporting. County attorney said not to touch vendor equipment on the right-of-way. Sparta city cameras are separate.

records.Primary_Reasons: Cost / low benefit after a trial; City manager and mayor non-renewal; Funds redirected inside PD
records.Summary: The City of Kingston will not renew its Flock Safety contract when the two-year 2024 deal expires in September 2026, the Mountain Press / Roane County News reported August 19. City Manager David Bolling said the two cameras were a trial and that the benefit did not justify the cost. Mayor Tim Neal said the decision is financial: about $6,000 a year, $12,300 for the two-year term.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Cameras remain through the September 2026 expiration. Cost-based non-renewal, not a privacy vote.

records.Summary: Monterey’s Law Committee voted Monday night, August 17, 2026, to recommend replacing most town Flock cameras with Axon readers. The Herald-Citizen quoted Lt. records.Summary: Wytheville Police Chief Joel Hash said in a news release around September 2, 2026 that the town is suspending its Flock system. records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Suspend, not a confirmed permanent terminate. Distinct from Wythe County sheriff terminate.

records.Primary_Reasons: Sheriff said Flock keeps a marketed Traffic Analytics dataset up to five years; Trust / contract dispute; May seek another vendor
records.Summary: Racine County Sheriff Christopher Schmaling ordered Flock cameras in the county taken down on September 4, 2026. He said the office believed scans were deleted after 30 days, then learned Flock generates a separate dataset and markets it through Traffic Analytics with retention up to five years. He said the office will cut ties and find another vendor. Wausau Pilot & Review reported Flock told the office the same thing was happening with Racine County data.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Sheriff ordered cameras down and said the county will find another vendor. Vendor-swap intent, not an ALPR ban. Traffic Analytics claim is the sheriff's account of what Flock confirmed, as reported.

records.Primary_Reasons: Loss of control over investigative data; Out-of-state open-records releases of search logs
records.Summary: All agencies in Fond du Lac County, including the sheriff's office, dropped or suspended Flock on September 4, 2026. CBS 58 quoted the county citing loss of control over investigative data. Wausau Pilot & Review said five Fond du Lac County agencies suspended programs after search data, including records tied to active investigations, was released by agencies in other states responding to open-records requests because Flock search logs are shared across a national network.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Coverage mixes drop/end and suspend. Catalogued as Suspended until a published terminate. County-level row for the five-agency cluster; unnamed city agencies not listed separately.

records.Summary: The Winnebago County Sheriff's Office and other agencies in the county suspended or ended Flock programs on September 4, 2026. CBS 58 quoted the county saying protecting the integrity of investigative data and public trust are paramount. Wausau Pilot & Review tied the move to out-of-state open-records releases of shared Flock search logs.
records.Incomplete_Exit_Notes: Coverage mixes ending and suspend. Catalogued as Suspended. Separate rows for Neenah and Menasha police.
